name: Iran war and oil
backstory: The Middle East conflict that began in early 2026 caused an unprecedented drop in global oil supply, with output down 12 mb/d [million barrels per day] in March. Prices jumped but not to record levels, because the world was oversupplied beforehand and inventories were drawn down. Tensions eased in June, then resumed.
today: WTI is 91.23 (+0.44%). Headlines say oil pared losses as Hormuz [the key shipping chokepoint for Gulf oil] and Houthi tensions persist. Trump says renewed Iran strikes are 'highly unlikely' if talks progress but he could still strike, and a former Biden advisor warns the war could return. The NY Fed piece says US stockpiles stopped falling in July, so the rest of the world is now running down its own inventories.

name: Central banks vs energy inflation
backstory: The oil shock pushed headline inflation up and central banks have to decide whether it stays temporary. After 2021, officials admitted they were wrong to call a supply shock transitory, so they are more cautious now.
today: The Bank of England raised Bank rate to 4%, its first hike since the Iran war began, and warned inflation will near 5%. ECB President Lagarde said euro-area October inflation was 4%, with energy inflation at 20.8% and core at 2.5%. She said the ECB decides meeting by meeting and cannot promise a December move. Headlines also say bond traders are backing off Fed hike bets.

name: AI trade jitters
backstory: Markets have leaned heavily on AI-linked mega-cap tech, so any doubt about AI spending or China competition hits the whole index. Headlines describe an AI selloff, concerns about AI spending, and warnings that the S&P 500 is dangerously exposed to AI.
today: The Nasdaq gained 1.09% and headlines say chip stocks led a tech rebound. A probe by Nvidia into its CEO's relationship with an alleged Chinese spy is in the news. DeepSeek headlines appear in the mix and may be older, so the timing is unclear.

name: US midterms and the dollar
backstory: The midterm elections produced what headlines call a Democratic rout, with voters blaming Trump for economic pain. Markets are now asking how a divided government would change tariffs, spending and the dollar.
today: Housing stocks rallied after the midterms and Treasury yields dipped, and gold is up 4% since the vote. HSBC says strong Democratic results could pressure the dollar near term, and the dollar index fell 0.15%. One analysis says Democrats have a chance to extract concessions from Trump and markets will dislike it. Another explains how Democrats might try to end Trump's tariffs.

name: Yen defense
backstory: A weak yen has pushed Japan to intervene [sell dollars to buy yen] in the foreign exchange market. Headlines say Japan spent a record $50 billion in a single day, and that a three-day intervention lifted the yen in summer.
today: USD/JPY rose 0.51% to 158.29. Japan's GPIF [the huge government pension fund] posted a $33.3 billion Q2 loss as a global bond selloff hit its foreign holdings. A shipper's profit was boosted by the weak yen.
